login.title: Sign in
login.heading: Welcome back
login.subheading: Sign in to manage your containers
setup.title: First setup
setup.heading: Set up D2HA
setup.code_help: To prove you own this server, enter the setup code printed in the container logs:
setup.username_help: 3–32 characters: letters, numbers, dot, dash or underscore.
help.password: At least 10 characters. A passphrase is easy to remember and hard to guess.
progress.background_hint: You can close this window: the update keeps going.
settings.totp_off: Two-factor authentication is off. D2HA can control Docker on this server: turn it on.
settings.totp_scan: Scan the QR code with an authenticator app (Aegis, Google Authenticator, 1Password…), then enter the code it shows.
settings.totp_manual: Or type this key in the app:
settings.totp_qr_alt: QR code for the authenticator app
settings.ha_step1: Install the D2HA integration. In Home Assistant 2026.11 or later: Settings → Marketplace → Add from link, enter https://github.com/arborae/ha-d2ha (type Integration), then Install and restart. In earlier versions add the same address in HACS as a custom repository (type Integration), download D2HA and restart.
settings.ha_step2: Create an access token below and copy it.
settings.ha_step3: In Home Assistant add the D2HA integration with the address of D2HA (http://127.0.0.1:12021 when it runs on the same server) and the token.
settings.token_once: Copy the token now: it is shown only once.
settings.token_active: A token is active: Home Assistant can connect.
settings.token_none: No token yet: Home Assistant cannot connect.
settings.token_regenerate_confirm: The current token stops working: Home Assistant will need the new one.
settings.token_revoke_confirm: Home Assistant will be disconnected until you create a new token.
settings.ha_visible_help: Hidden containers get no entity in Home Assistant. Changes apply at the next refresh of the integration.
settings.notify_missing: Not configured. Set D2HA_TELEGRAM_TOKEN (the token of your bot, from @BotFather) and D2HA_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID (the chat that receives the messages) in the environment of D2HA, then restart it.
settings.notify_ready: Telegram is configured. Choose what deserves a message:
settings.notify_updates: New updates (one message per new version)
settings.notify_events_help: Stopped and unhealthy containers come from the Docker events: with a socket proxy, allow EVENTS.
flash.welcome: Account created. Next: turn on two-factor authentication and connect Home Assistant.
flash.password_changed: Password changed. Other devices have been signed out.
flash.totp_enabled: Two-factor authentication is on. Other devices have been signed out.
error.too_many_attempts: Too many attempts. Try again in a few minutes.
error.setup_code: The setup code is not correct.
error.password_short: The password must have at least 10 characters.
error.password_weak: This password is too easy to guess.
error.current_password: The current password is not correct.
error.totp_code: The code is not valid. Check the time of your phone and try again.
error.not_found: Container not found: it may have been removed.
error.no_tag: This container runs an image without a tag, so it cannot be updated.
error.self_update: D2HA cannot update itself: use docker compose pull and docker compose up -d.
error.recreate_failed: The new container did not start: the previous one has been restored.
error.proxy_update: D2HA reaches Docker through this container, so it cannot update it: use docker compose pull and docker compose up -d.
error.rate_limited: Too many requests: wait a moment.
error.telegram: Telegram did not take the message: {detail}
api.rate_limited: Too many requests: wait a moment.
api.proxy_update: D2HA cannot update the proxy it uses to reach Docker.
js.self: This is D2HA: update it with docker compose pull.
js.proxy: D2HA reaches Docker through this container: update it with docker compose pull.
js.confirm.update.title: Update {name}?
js.confirm.update.text: The new image is downloaded first, then the container is recreated with the same settings. The service is offline for a few seconds; if the new container does not start, the previous one is restored.
js.confirm.update.breaking: The release notes contain breaking changes: read them before updating.
js.confirm.update_all.title: Update {n} containers?
js.confirm.update_all.text: Containers are updated one at a time, each with its own restart of a few seconds.
js.confirm.prune.title: Delete unused images?
js.confirm.prune.text: {n} images are not used by any container. They will be deleted; they can be downloaded again when needed.
js.progress.title: Updating {name}
js.notes.title: {name} · {version}
notify.breaking: Breaking changes: read the notes before updating
notify.oom: Out of memory: the kernel stopped it.
